items.title: In Numbers: How Different Religions May Grow Over The Next 50 Years
points: The world's religious composition is expected to change significantly over the next five decades, with Muslims projected to grow faster than any other major religious group.

According to projections by Pew Research Center, the global Muslim population is expected to increase by 80 per cent between 2020 and 2070, far outpacing overall world population growth of 29 per cent during the same period.
Christians are projected to grow by 30 per cent, while Hindus are expected to grow by 17 per cent.
In contrast, Buddhist populations are projected to shrink by 23 per cent, and the number of religiously unaffiliated people is expected to decline by 10 per cent.

While fertility rates are projected to decline across nearly all religious groups over the coming decades, Muslims are expected to retain the highest fertility rate among major religions, as per Pew Research Center.

items.title: When Was Roblox Made? History of Roblox
points: Roblox is one of the biggest platforms with over seven million experiences and 150 million+ daily active users, but it wasn’t always the platform we know today.
Players always wonder when Roblox was created, and what its history has been.
But before players could explore experiences like Brookhaven, Blox Fruits, and Adopt Me, Roblox started as a simple virtual world builder.
In 1989, David Baszucki founded Knowledge Revolution, a company that made educational physics software.

In 2003, Baszucki and Cassel began working on a virtual environment builder called DynaBlocks, which was a platform that was designed around simulated physics and allowed users to create their own digital worlds.
In January 2004, they finalised the name Roblox, combining the words ‘robots’ and ‘blocks’.
After going through several testing phases, Roblox was finally released on September 1, 2006, along with Roblox Studio.
David Baszucki and Erik Cassel started working on Roblox in 2003.

items.title: A big shift for gold trading? JPMorgan, HSBC and StoneX complete first digital gold deals- What to know
points: Some of the world's biggest banks have completed their first live trades using a new form of digital gold in London, marking a potential turning point for the global bullion market.

The World Gold Council (WGC) said the transactions mark the first time major banks have tested the system in real market deals.
The transactions were carried out under the WGC's Wholesale Digital Gold initiative, which aims to modernise the way gold is owned, transferred and used by large financial institutions.
The pilot used standard 400-ounce London Good Delivery gold bars.

points: Oppo's K14 5G and K14x 5G (pictured) are eligible for the update Oppo is continuing its ColorOS 17 rollout in India, with the K14 5G, K14x 5G, F31 5G and F33 5G now reportedly receiving the stable update.

According to a report by The Tech Outlook, Oppo has begun rolling out ColorOS 17 for the K14 5G, K14x 5G, F31 5G and F33 5G in India.
ColorOS 17 is based on Android 17 and brings changes to the interface, along with improvements to animations and overall performance.

Oppo's Luminous Rendering Engine is intended to make scrolling and transitions smoother, while the Laminar Flow Engine optimises resource management to improve app responsiveness and keep apps running in the background.
There are also several AI additions like AI Mind Space, which helps users save and organise information, while AI Mind Pilot uses this information to handle requests.

items.title: UK FCA Calls for Stricter DeFi Regulations After $6.3 Billion Binance Hack
points: As reported by the Financial Times on November 26, the authority plans to regulate various blockchain-enabled financial activities in its soon-to-be-launched framework, including platforms that are meant to function without a centralised controlling authority.

The officials from the FCA explained that their decision to adopt this method was partly because of the challenges that come with the recovery of stolen cryptocurrencies that have gone through decentralised trading platforms.

In particular, regulators have cited the October 29 security breach at Binance, where roughly $6.3 billion (roughly Rs 58,268.7 crore) worth of cryptocurrencies were compromised, as a way that decentralised platforms could be utilised in order to launder…

According to Blockchain intelligence company Elliptic, there were 1,650 Bitcoins worth $124 million (roughly Rs 1,146.8 crore) that had been earned through conversion of other cryptocurrencies as of November 6.
Jane Moore, chief of Payments and Digital Assets at the FCA, appealed for solutions that can tackle this kind of threat to money laundering.

items.title: Haier Civic AI Maxx Robot Vacuum Cleaner With 8,000Pa Suction Launched in India: Price, Features
points: Haier has launched the Haier Civic AI Maxx robot vacuum cleaner in India.
The new robotic vacuum cleaner features LDS laser navigation and offers an 8,000Pa suction system.

After washing, the dock dries the mops with a 45-degree Celsius hot-air drying system.

items.title: Four newborn lion cubs die after pregnant lionesses rescued ahead of Gujarat pilgrimage
points: Four newborn lion cubs have died at Gujarat’s Sakkarbaug Zoological Garden after two pregnant lionesses rescued from the Girnar Wildlife Sanctuary ahead of the annual Lili Parikrama were brought to the zoo.
The deaths have raised questions among wildlife experts over the Forest Department’s practice of capturing and confining lions to keep them away from the pilgrimage route.
Principal chief conservator of forests (wildlife) and chief wildlife warden of Gujarat Jaipal Singh said that two lionesses were rescued and brought to Sakkarbaug Zoo.
Singh said in a statement that one of the lionesses had been rescued ahead of the Parikrama with a deep wound on her back that was infested with maggots.
Considering her serious condition, she was rescued and brought to Sakkarbaug Zoological Garden for treatment,” Singh said.
However, Forest department officials said at least 30 lions were rescued ahead of the five-day Parikrama, held from November 20 to 24, and kept at four separate locations.

items.title: Stipend for unemployed graduates, state jobs for Agniveers, return of laptop scheme in SP poll manifesto
points: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Thursday unveiled its poll manifesto ahead of the 2027 Assembly polls in Uttar Pradesh, with caste census and government jobs in focus.
In the manifesto, titled ‘PDA Ka Prannpatra’, SP has promised 50 per cent reservation for PDA communities in government contracts, caste census as well as 25 lakh government jobs over five years.

SP chief Yadav coined the term ‘PDA’, defining it as standing for the “Pichhda, Dalit, and Alpsankhyak (Backward classes, Dalits, and Minorities).” Yadav has positioned the ‘PDA’ communities at the core of his political strategy in UP.
The party has also assured a monthly allowance of ₹5,000 to unemployed graduates until they secure employment.
Yadav, who is also an from UP's Kannauj, said the party would bring back the laptop distribution scheme for students who pass Class 12.
The Free Laptop Distribution Scheme had first been introduced in 2012 in UP by the then SP government led by Yadav.

Pending Traffic Challans To Make Car Insurance Costlier :Government's New Proposal
points: A speeding ticket could eventually cost more than the fine printed on the challan.
The road transport ministry is reportedly studying a plan to link motor insurance premiums to traffic violations recorded against vehicle owners during the previous year.
If implemented, repeated offenders could end up paying more when they renew insurance for their cars or two-wheelers.
The reported move is part of a broader government effort to reduce the number of uninsured vehicles on the roads.
Other ideas under consideration include longer-duration insurance policies and a limited trial of refusing fuel to vehicles without valid insurance.
At present, a normal traffic challan and a motor insurance renewal are largely separate transactions.
A working group set up by insurance regulator IRDAI had proposed a traffic-violation premium in 2021 and recommended using a points-based approach.
Another proposal involves a 'no insurance, no fuel' pilot at ten petrol pumps equipped with automatic number plate recognition cameras: five each in Haryana and Uttar Pradesh.

items.title: China Urges Safety For Black Sea Shipping As EU Calls It The World’s Deadliest Maritime Route
points: Black Sea shipping came into focus at the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) on November 23, 2026, as China called for the protection of merchant vessels and port facilities in the region.
China’s UN Ambassador Fu Cong spoke at a high-level council session that focused on energy infrastructure and the Black Sea’s role in world food supply.
Officials stated that Ukrainian grain exports have fallen by roughly 25% compared to last year, while World Food Programme shipments from the region have dropped by more than half.
Ambassador Fu Cong told the council that cargo ships in the region have come under attack many times over a long period, while ports in Russia and Ukraine have suffered damage too.
Recent strikes on Russian ships in other seas were also a matter of concern for China, the diplomat added during his address.
The head of the European Union’s delegation to the UN told the council that the Black Sea is now the deadliest maritime route in the world.

items.title: France Frees Suspected Russian Shadow Fleet Tanker DF Peak After Owner Reportedly Pays €1 Million Penalty
points: Suspected Russian shadow fleet tanker DF Peak will be allowed to leave French waters after a court on the French island of Réunion in the Indian Ocean convicted its owner for failing to prove the ship’s flag.
The public prosecutor’s office in Réunion said in a statement that the company owning the vessel was convicted on November 24, 2026 under a guilty-plea procedure.
Maritime reports identify the vessel as a crude oil tanker built in 2007, linked to Russia’s state-owned shipping giant Sovcomflot.
It was later renamed from Kaliningrad in June 2024 and transferred to a Hong Kong-registered company, and is on the European Union’s sanctions list of around 700 vessels.
Prosecutors did not disclose the amount in their statement, but the penalty was reportedly set at €1 million to match the value of the ship.
The French Navy boarded DF Peak on October 12, 2026, in international waters more than 450 nautical miles south of Réunion.

items.title: China To Open Its 10,000-Ton Type 055 Destroyer To Public For The First Time At Zhuhai Airshow
points: The Type 055 destroyer of China’s navy will be opened to public tours for the first time at Airshow China in the city of Zhuhai next month.
China’s People’s Liberation Army (PLA) Navy shared the plan on November 23, 2026, for the 16th edition of the country’s international aviation and aerospace exhibition.
The week-long show will take place between December 7 and 13 in the port city that lies in Guangdong province of southern China.
Members of the public will get a chance to step aboard this 10,000-tonne-class warship that China built on its own during the show.
Visitors can book reservations in advance and board the vessels from the Gaolan Port, located roughly 30 kilometres west of the main airshow grounds at Jinwan Airport.
The navy has not revealed which Type 055 destroyer will be on show and has only called it a ‘mysterious 10,000-ton large destroyer’.

items.title: US State New York Awards $228 Million To Five Port Projects To Create 1000 Jobs
points: New York state in the US has handed out $228 million for five projects at its ports and shipyards, which is expected to boost cargo handling, vessel building and offshore wind work on its waterfronts.

The $228 million award is part of New York’s broader $500 million commitment to build out a domestic offshore wind supply chain and modernise its old port facilities, with another $72 million set aside for the second funding round.
Announcing the awards on November 20, 2026, Governor Kathy Hochul said that these projects will create over 1000 jobs for the state.
A whopping $100 million out of the total has gone to the Port of Coeymans on the Hudson River for a new heavy-lift wharf and a fabrication facility.

Beacon Island near Albany will be turned into a new multi-use marine hub called the Empire Terminal after the Port of Albany secured $94.8 million, and the site will get an ultra-heavy-capacity wharf.

items.title: French Shipyard Delivers 216,638-Ton MSC World Asia As Tenth Largest Cruise Ship Ever Built
points: MSC World Asia has joined the MSC Cruises fleet after the cruise line took delivery of the new ship from the Chantiers de l’Atlantique shipyard in Saint-Nazaire, France, on November 25, 2026.

The vessel is the 24th ship in the company’s fleet and the third ship of its World Class series of cruise ships, and the 20th vessel that the French shipyard has built for the cruise line over a partnership lasting more than 25 years.
Construction of MSC World Asia brought together more than 500 French suppliers over more than two years of work, the cruise line said.
The 216,638-ton vessel is reportedly the tenth largest cruise ship ever built and is smaller than only nine Royal Caribbean ships of the Icon and Oasis classes.
It is 1093 feet long and 154 feet wide, which matches the size of the two World Class ships already in service.

items.title: US Court Refuses To Free Tanker That Capsized American Heritage As Owners Seek $24.5 Million Cap
points: Tanker Atlantic Asphalt must remain under arrest in New Orleans after a US federal judge refused to release the vessel that struck and capsized the riverboat American Heritage on the Mississippi River.
US District Judge Wendy Vitter turned down the request on November 23, 2026, at a hearing on the first arguments from lawyers for the tanker’s owner and operator.
The tanker struck the docked riverboat at the city’s port on November 13, causing the cruise vessel to capsize at the dock.
Lawyers for the owner, Nave Shipping of Liberia and the operator, Thome Ship Management of Singapore, told the court that the tanker was in good order and condition.
A London-based ship valuer has valued the tanker at $24.5 million before the crash, and this amount will be the maximum payout if the limit stays in place.
The Marshall Islands-flagged Atlantic Asphalt was built in 2017 and has faced earlier technical problems, US Coast Guard records show.

items.title: US Shipbuilder HII Wins $186 Million For Royal Navy Mine-Hunting Underwater Drones
points: REMUS 620 underwater drones will hunt sea mines for Britain’s Royal Navy after the UK Ministry of Defence awarded US shipbuilder HII a £142 million contract for the unmanned vehicles.
On November 24, 2026, HII announced that the contract is worth about $186 million.
The deal was handed out by the UK’s National Armaments Director Group (NADG) for the Mine-Hunting Capability (MHC) programme of the Royal Navy, which picked HII after an open international contest.

The contract also builds on the Royal Navy’s existing fleet of smaller REMUS 100 and REMUS 300 underwater vehicles, giving British forces a larger and longer-range drone capable of scanning wider areas of the seabed in a single mission.
HII called it the biggest overseas order its unmanned systems business has won in its 25 years.
Under the Royal Navy’s Hybrid Navy approach of mixing crewed and uncrewed assets, the drones will be deployed from offshore support ships acting as motherships.

items.title: French Navy Seizes 3.3 Tonnes Of Methamphetamine From Flagless Tanker In North Pacific
points: The French Navy has seized more than 3.3 tonnes of methamphetamine from a small tanker that was sailing without a flag in the North Pacific Ocean.
The French Pacific Command informed that a navy unit stopped the stateless vessel on November 20, 2026, in waters lying beyond those controlled by French Polynesia.
Sailors from a French frigate boarded the suspect tanker and took control of it as allowed by the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).

In the recent bust, the French frigate’s own helicopter backed the boarding team from the air while a Falcon 50 jet of the French forces in French Polynesia and a US Coast Guard patrol plane also took part.
The French Navy seized more than 9.1 tonnes of cocaine in the South Pacific.
The first operation happened on January 16, 2026, when a French Navy ship stopped a suspicious vessel identified as the MV Raider.

items.title: 'Excellent trade deal with US': MEA official says India tariffs will be lower than most others
points: Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh said on Thursday that the tariffs faced by India after a trade deal with the US will be lower when compared to duties on countries such as Vietnam and Bangladesh.
He also praised India's negotiations with the US, stating that New Delhi had negotiated an "excellent trade deal" with Washington on tariffs.

This comes after the US on Wednesday proposed a tariff of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods, following an investigation into what Washington described as "structural excess capacity" in 16 major economies.
Furthermore, the 17 per cent is lower than the 18 per cent the two nations agreed on in a framework for the deal in February.
Meanwhile, Bangladesh, Thailand, Malaysia, Cambodia and Indonesia face 18 per cent.

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer announced the findings of the investigations, identifying India, China, Bangladesh, the European Union (EU), Japan, South Korea, Singapore, and Vietnam among the economies under scrutiny.

items.title: Singapore’s PIL Completes China’s First Liquefied Bio-Methane Bunkering At Qingdao
points: Pacific International Lines (PIL) has carried out the first-ever bunkering of liquefied bio-methane (LBM) for an internationally trading ship in China by fuelling its container ship Kota Odyssey at Qingdao Port.
Qingdao Port Group partnered with the carrier for the operation, in which the LNG dual-fuel vessel was supplied with the ISCC-certified fuel by truck at the QQCTN terminal.
The operation also marked the first time the Singapore-based carrier had used LBM fuel on any of its ships.
This particular batch could reduce carbon emissions by over 70 per cent compared with conventional fuel oil on a well-to-wake basis, while the cut against fossil LNG is estimated at 70%.
Energy business department head Yijie Zhang of Ark Intelligence at Qingdao Port called the maiden biomethane bunkering service a ‘major milestone’ for the green shipping transition of the country.

The operation supports PIL’s broader goal of reaching net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, as the Singapore carrier gradually replaces older ships with modern vessels that can run on cleaner fuels.

points: Cruise ship Viking Libra has been delivered to Viking by Italian shipbuilder Fincantieri, thereby giving the cruise line what it calls the world’s first hydrogen-powered cruise ship.
The 239-metre newbuild has a gross tonnage of around 54300 and offers 998 guest berths spread across 499 cabins.
Viking Libra is considered a sister ship of the existing Viking ocean fleet, but it is fitted with a hybrid propulsion system based partly on liquefied hydrogen and fuel cells.
It is part of a massive expansion plan that will see Fincantieri deliver a total of 26 ocean ships to Viking by 2032, along with 10 other vessels, bringing the company’s total fleet over 100 ships.
Viking Libra was floated out at the same yard in March 2026, which marked the start of the final stage of its construction.
The ship is expected to begin operating on hydrogen in 2027 along with Viking Astrea, which is the next ocean ship of the cruise line and will carry the same hybrid propulsion system.

items.title: Japan’s NYK Line And Partners Develop Tech To Measure Ship Emissions From A Distance
points: NYK Line of Japan has joined hands with seven organisations in the country to build a technology that can measure greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions of ships from a distance without touching them.
The agreement for the same was signed on November 25, 2026, and Yokohama Port will be the main site for the trials.
The initiative has been named True Emission Eye Maritime and aims to measure, visualise and quantify the emissions coming out of vessels.
Banking major MUFG Bank and Nagoya Electric Works are among the partners, as are ArkEdge Space and construction firm Shimizu Corporation.
Readings from the exhaust are then put together with the distance to the ship and the weather at the time to work out how much it emits.
At Yokohama Port, the team captured infrared images of ship exhaust from spots like a pier and the skywalk of the Yokohama Bay Bridge, which are now being matched against vessel data.

points: Ultraviolette Automotive has committed an investment of Rs 779 crores towards setting up a new manufacturing facility in Hosur, Tamil Nadu.
Called BIGGA (Big Global Ambition), the facility is planned to have an annual production capacity of 2.5 lakh units, which will be achieved in phases.
The infrastructure will also allow the company to scale capacity to 5 lakh units in the future.
The new plant will manufacture Ultraviolette’s upcoming electric two-wheelers, including the Tesseract electric scooter and Shockwave electric motorcycle.
Ultraviolette BIGGA factory: Manufacturing and employment The Hosur facility will operate alongside the company’s existing manufacturing operations in Bengaluru, Karnataka.
The project is expected to generate around 2,000 jobs initially, with further employment opportunities planned over the next five years.
The factory will use Industry 4.0 manufacturing technologies, including collaborative robotics, automated production systems, vision-based inspection and digital quality management.

Commenting on the expansion, Ultraviolette co-founder and CEO Narayan Subramaniam highlighted Hosur’s established automotive supplier network and its proximity to the company’s research and development operations.

items.title: Indian banks seek RBI intervention as dollar surplus pushes up rupee forward premiums
points: Indian lenders have sought RBI intervention to absorb surplus dollars as rising overnight FX swap rates put upward pressure on rupee forward premiums.
Indian lenders have sought the central bank's intervention in managing a ​dollar surplus that is pushing up overnight FX swap rates ‌and rupee forward premiums, three bankers said.

Foreign investors ​have poured nearly $15 billion into Indian equities ⁠this month, adding to excess dollar liquidity created by previously done sell-buy swaps conducted by the Reserve Bank of India ‌to manage rupee liquidity.

The dollar surplus has driven up overnight dollar/rupee swap rates, which ‌in turn is putting upward pressure on ‌forward premiums, ⁠the bankers, who did not want ⁠to identified since they are not authorised to speak to the media, said.

"The excess dollar liquidity and the market distortions it is ​causing could worsen ‌with month-end approaching, and the situation will become more acute towards the quarter-end," a treasury official at a private sector bank said.

items.title: Mumbai Police issues LOCs against CJP's Saurav Das, Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka over Dadar protest last month
points: Mumbai Police has issued look-out circulars against Cockroach Janta Party leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, seven weeks after the organisation's protest in Shivaji Park on October 2.

items.title: Mediation in shipping disputes: an opportunity worth taking
points: Mediation is a confidential process in which an independent mediator helps the parties negotiate a settlement.
Courts are giving mediation greater weight Mediation in English court proceedings gained momentum in 1996, when the Central London County Court introduced its first mediation scheme.
The Civil Procedure Rules 1998, which overhauled litigation procedures in England, actively encouraged mediation.
In Churchill v Merthyr Tydfil Borough Council [2023] EWCA Civ 1416, the Court of Appeal confirmed that courts can order parties to attempt alternative dispute resolution (ADR), including mediation.
The Civil Procedure Rules were amended with effect from 1 October 2024 to reflect that ruling, with CPR 1.4 and 3.1 expressly addressing the court’s role in ordering ADR.
In DKH Retail Ltd v City Football Group [2024] EWHC 3231 (Ch), the court ordered mediation despite the defendant’s objections that it was too late and had no realistic prospect of success.
Online mediation, which grew out of necessity during the COVID-19 lockdowns, also remains popular.

What are Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) and Ultra Large Crude Carrier (ULCC)?
points: A Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) is a crude-oil tanker with a deadweight tonnage ranging between 200,000–320,000 DWT.
An Ultra Large Crude Carrier (ULCC) is larger, with a DWT of 320,000 to 550,000 metric tons.
Main role Long-haul crude-oil transportation Very large-volume crude-oil transportation on suitable routes Port access Requires deepwater terminals More restricted; cannot call at U.S. coastal ports.
As mentioned above, a Very Large Crude Carrier is a tanker that is specifically designed to transport unrefined petroleum.

An Ultra Large Crude Carrier is an ever bigger class of crude oil tanker that can accommodate nearly 3 million barrels of crude oil, though the actual cargo volume depends on the density of the crude and also the vessel loading plan.
The largest Ultra Large Crude Carrier ever built was the Seawise Giant, later named as Knock Nevis and Mont.
Currently, the biggest ULCCs are the 4 TI-Class supertankers, namely the TI Africa, TI Europe, TI Oceania and TI Asia.

Previously, the hybrid version was offered from the VX variant, which started at Rs 26.76 lakh.
The new entry-level hybrid variant brings down the starting price of the hybrid range by Rs 6.77 lakh.
Toyota Innova Hycross facelift powertrain and specifications The strong hybrid version continues with a 1987cc, four-cylinder petrol engine paired with an electric motor.
The combined system produces 197 HP and 206 Nm of torque, with power delivered to the front wheels through an e-CVT gearbox.
It produces 173 HP and 206 Nm and comes paired with a CVT gearbox.

items.title: Paradip Port rescues 27 seafarers; reports major cargo growth | The Port Report #40
Honda Alpha Interior Revealed Ahead Of December 2 India Debut
points: The midsize electric SUV will make its India debut on December 2, marking the Japanese carmaker’s entry into the country’s all-electric passenger vehicle segment.
The exterior design was previously previewed through the 0 α concept at the Japan Mobility Show in October 2025.
Honda Alpha interior: Design and features The cabin sketch shows a dual-tone black and off-white theme, with several elements appearing familiar from the Honda City and Elevate.
Honda Alpha exterior design previewed The exterior design sketch indicates that the production version will retain several styling elements of the 0 α concept.
However, the battery pack is expected to be in the 65kWh-75kWh range, based on earlier indications from Honda officials.

For reference, electric SUVs with similarly sized battery packs typically offer claimed ranges in the 400-500km bracket, although the Alpha’s final certified figures will be revealed closer to its launch.
The Honda Alpha is expected to be priced between Rs 15 lakhs and Rs 25 lakhs (ex-showroom).

items.title: Honda CB500 Full Specifications Revealed, Gets 28 BHP And 43 Nm
points: Honda has revealed the complete specifications and feature list of the newly launched CB500, giving buyers a better understanding of its retro roadster.
The motorcycle was recently launched in India with prices starting at Rs 2.75 lakh (ex-showroom), and is available in three variants.
The Honda CB500 is powered by a 501.7cc, single-cylinder, air-cooled engine with an oil cooler.
It produces 28.14 PS at 5,250 RPM and 43.3 Nm of torque at 3,750 RPM.
In terms of dimensions, the Honda CB500 weighs 189 kg (kerb) and gets 168 mm of ground clearance.
Honda offers the CB500 in three variants, with prices starting at Rs 2.75 lakh (ex-showroom).
The entry-level Alloy variant is priced at Rs 2.75 lakh, while the Spoke variant costs Rs 3 lakh.
The range-topping Spoke with Stripe variant is priced at Rs 3.02 lakh.

items.title: Tata Motors Price Hike December 2026: Prices To Rise By 0.5%
points: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles (TMPV) will increase prices across its internal combustion engine (ICE) and electric vehicle (EV) range by up to 0.5 percent from December 1, 2026.
The price adjustment will apply across the portfolio, although the extent of the increase will differ depending on the model and variant.
Tata Motors price hike December 2026: What to expect Tata Motors is yet to publish the revised price list for its vehicles.
Based on the announced increase, buyers can expect prices to go up by approximately Rs 2384 to Rs 14,645, depending on the model and variant.
This marks Tata Motors’ third price hike in 2026.
Other carmakers announcing price hikes Tata Motors is among several manufacturers revising vehicle prices around the end of 2026.
Hyundai has announced an increase for select models from December, while Audi will implement a price hike of up to 2 percent from January 2027.
The revised Tata Motors price list is expected to be announced closer to the implementation date.

items.title: JSW Motors Logo Revealed Ahead Of December 3 Brand Debut
points: JSW Motors has revealed its brand logo ahead of its official debut scheduled for December 3, 2026.
The logo will make its first appearance on the JSW Combat, the company’s debut SUV, which is also scheduled to be unveiled on December 3.
JSW Combat SUV launch and powertrain details JSW Motors will introduce its first product, the Combat, alongside its brand debut on December 3.
The setup is likely to comprise a 1.5-litre, four-cylinder, direct-injection turbo-petrol engine, two electric motors mounted at the front and an 18.4kWh battery pack.
The combined output is expected to be around 360 HP and 610 Nm, with power delivered to the front wheels through a 3-speed dedicated hybrid transmission.
For reference, the international-spec version of this powertrain is claimed to offer an NEDC-certified electric-only range of 90 km and a combined driving range of up to 1200 km.

items.title: Audi Car Prices To Increase By Up To 2% From January 2027
points: Audi India will revise prices across its model range by up to 2 percent from January 1, 2027.
The company had implemented a similar price revision of up to 2 percent in April 2026.
The January adjustment will therefore mark its second price hike during FY2027.
Audi price hike January 2027: What to expect The upcoming revision is expected to translate into an increase of approximately Rs 1.04 lakhs to Rs 4.68 lakhs, depending on the model and variant.
Audi is yet to announce the revised ex-showroom prices, which will be communicated in January 2027.
Commenting on the decision, Balbir Singh Dhillon, Brand Director, Audi India, said the revision was necessary to manage increasing input costs and ensure the long-term sustainability of the business.
Audi’s current India portfolio starts with the Q3 SUV, priced at Rs 51.99 lakhs, while the RS Q8 sits at the top of the range with a starting price of Rs 2.34 crores (ex-showroom).

items.title: Hyundai Car Prices To Increase By Up To Rs. 8000 In December 2026
points: Hyundai will increase prices of select cars in its Indian portfolio from December 1, 2026.
The company has announced that the revision will be limited to Rs 8000, depending on the model and variant.
Hyundai price hike December 2026: Models affected Hyundai has not yet disclosed the complete list of models and variants that will receive a price revision.
The company’s current Indian lineup includes the Grand i10 Nios, i20, Aura, Exter, Venue, Verna, Creta, Alcazar, Tucson and IONIQ 5, along with other offerings.
Fourth Hyundai price hike in 2026 This will be Hyundai’s fourth price revision in the Indian market this year.
The company had previously increased prices in January, June and September 2026, citing higher input costs on those occasions as well.
Maruti Suzuki has also implemented four price increases in 2026, while Tata Motors and Audi are among the other brands that have announced price revisions.

items.title: Kia Seltos Petrol DCT: A Diwali Getaway Via Ganga Expressway
points: We drove the turbo-petrol Seltos to Uttar Pradesh over the Diwali break, covering city traffic and open highways to see how it performs as a family road-trip car.
Road trips are a good way to understand a car beyond its feature list and specification sheet.
Over the Diwali break, I drove the Kia Seltos 1.5-litre turbo-petrol DCT from Delhi to my hometown in Uttar Pradesh, taking the Ganga Expressway for most of the highway journey.
The trip involved everything from bumper-to-bumper traffic while exiting Delhi to long, uninterrupted stretches of expressway driving.
The Seltos returned an indicated fuel efficiency of around 15.5 km/l in a mix of city and highway driving.
The turbo-petrol engine comes into its own on the expressway The Seltos is powered by a 1.5-litre turbocharged petrol engine that produces 160 PS and 253 Nm of torque.
Even at 120 km/hr, which is the speed limit on the Ganga Expressway, the engine was spinning at approximately 2100 RPM.

items.title: India–Cyprus Maritime Business Forum strengthens Bilateral Cooperation in Shipping and Maritime Sector
MG Windsor Facelift In 2027 To Get Larger 61kWh Battery
points: MG Motor India is preparing a facelift for the Windsor EV, which is expected to arrive in 2027.
The Windsor was launched in India in 2024 and has since become MG’s highest-selling model in the country.
It was initially offered with a 38kWh battery, while a larger 52.9kWh option was added in 2025.
The model has crossed 80,000 units in cumulative sales in 2026, making it an important product for the brand’s Indian operations.
MG Windsor facelift expected to get 61kWh battery The biggest mechanical change expected on the facelifted Windsor is a new 61kWh battery pack.
For reference, the existing 38kWh version has an ARAI-certified range of 332 km, while the 52.9kWh variant is rated at 449 km on a single charge.
If introduced, the 61kWh battery option would give the Windsor a larger battery capacity than several electric vehicles in its price segment.
MG Windsor facelift expected to command a higher price The current MG Windsor is priced between Rs 14.85 lakhs and Rs 19.15 lakhs (ex-showroom).

items.title: Maruti Suzuki Car Price Hike November 2026: Fourth Increase This Year
points: Maruti Suzuki has announced another price increase across its passenger vehicle range, marking the fourth revision in 2026.
Effective November 22, the latest hike translates to an average increase of around 0.31 percent, although the actual change will vary depending on the model.
Maruti Suzuki car prices increased for fourth time in 2026 The latest revision follows three price increases announced by Maruti Suzuki earlier in 2026.
The company increased prices by up to Rs 30,000 in June, followed by another revision in August and a hike of up to Rs 20,000 in September.
During its Q2 FY2027 earnings call, Maruti Suzuki management indicated that additional increases could be considered depending on the movement of input costs over the coming months.
However, its net profit declined 26.36 percent year-on-year to Rs 2466.1 crore.
These costs accounted for 79.9 percent of Maruti Suzuki’s net sales in Q2 FY2027, compared to 75.7 percent during the same period last year.

New Honda Avancier Debuts With Next-Gen Hybrid Technology
points: Honda has unveiled the second generation Avancier, introducing a new hybrid powertrain and updated vehicle technologies.

The three-row SUV is the first model to use the Japanese carmaker’s next-generation hybrid platform, which brings improvements to engine efficiency, the electric drive unit and vehicle control systems.
The original Avancier was introduced over a decade ago as Honda’s flagship SUV for China.
New Honda Avancier hybrid powertrain and technology Honda has not disclosed the complete technical specifications of the new Avancier’s hybrid powertrain.
The Avancier also gets Honda’s S+ Shift technology, which simulates gear changes in a hybrid powertrain.

It is designed to make acceleration feel more engaging by replicating the response of a conventional stepped transmission.\ New Honda Avancier exterior design The second-generation Avancier introduces Honda’s new ‘Grand-Journey’ design language.
The tailgate features the Honda emblem and an Avancier lettering badge, while a roof-mounted spoiler incorporates an integrated stop lamp.

BYD Ti7 Banned From EU Sales After JLR Defender Design Dispute
points: A court in the Netherlands has ruled against BYD in a design infringement case involving its Ti7 SUV and Jaguar Land Rover’s Defender.
The district court in The Hague has ordered BYD not to sell the Ti7 in the European Union, following a complaint filed by JLR over alleged similarities between the two SUVs.
The legal action was initiated after BYD opened order books for the Ti7 in the UK, with customer deliveries scheduled to begin in January 2027.
In its ruling, the Dutch court observed that the Ti7 incorporates several distinctive design elements associated with the Defender.
The court has directed that the sales restriction will come into effect one week after the ruling, as BYD does not currently have concrete plans to introduce the Ti7 in the European Union.
BYD Ti7 UK Launch And Pricing BYD introduced the Ti7 in the UK in July 2026, with prices starting at £47,995 (approximately Rs 59.92 lakhs).

‘105 days of Operation Lotus’: Opposition targets Centre over special Parliament sitting amid delimitation bill buzz
points: Opposition leaders have condemned the government's initiative to convene a special sitting of Parliament on November 30.
They allege that this move aims to secure the necessary numbers for the delimitation-linked Constitution amendment Bill.
Various opposition parties have expressed concerns about the implications for parliamentary democracy.
The Congress and CPI(M) particularly highlight the government’s motives behind this political maneuvering.

items.title: 'Wish Akhilesh spent 6 months in jail': Azam Khan quips; gets witty reply from SP chief
points: Azam Khan openly wished that Akhilesh Yadav would spend time in prison to truly grasp its harsh realities.

During the launch of the SP manifesto for the upcoming elections, Khan shared his emotional turmoil over being distanced from his son and the sleepless nights spent worrying about his son's fate amid transfers.

items.title: CM Yogi Adityanath accuses opposition of weakening Constitution, misleading people with ‘red book’
points: Yogi Adityanath addressed a Constitution Day programme in Lucknow, criticizing opposition parties for weakening democratic institutions.
He specifically accused the Congress of disrespecting Dr. BR Ambedkar and undermining the Constitution.
Adityanath announced beautification projects at nearly 4,000 Ambedkar sites as part of a development scheme.
Furthermore, he highlighted the importance of voting rights granted to all citizens since the Constitution's enforcement.

items.title: SC orders separate warning labels for high sugar, salt and fat in packaged food
points: The Supreme Court has ordered food safety authorities to introduce clear warning labels indicating high levels of sugar, salt, and fat.
Food manufacturers must revise their packaging within a year to include these warnings, which should be prominently displayed.
The court raised issues regarding inconsistent standards among global food companies and emphasized that all manufacturers, regardless of size, should adhere to the new labeling regulations.

items.title: 'INSIGHT: The DNA of Success': Sadhguru inaugurates 15th edition of business leadership programme
points: Sadhguru inaugurated the 15th edition of the INSIGHT business leadership programme at Isha Yoga Center.
More than 200 business owners and executives participated to discuss business growth, leadership, and entrepreneurship.
Notable speakers included Sudipta Bhattacharya, Dr Sangita Reddy, and Abhimanyu Munjal, among others.
Sadhguru emphasized the importance of human intelligence and its role in business and leadership.
The three-day event will focus on discussions about leadership, decision-making, and individual development.

items.title: India-Cyprus seek maritime synergy, look to navigate West Asia disruptions
points: Marina Hadjimanolis, Cyprus’s Deputy Shipping Minister, emphasized the promising prospects of the India-Middle East-Europe-Economic Corridor for cooperative ventures.
Both nations are pursuing sustainable partnerships in areas such as shipping and maritime education.
Cypriot shipping firms highly value the expertise of Indian seafarers.
Despite prevailing geopolitical challenges, efforts are ongoing to advance the IMEC initiative, highlighting the need for further collaboration to maximize mutual benefits.

items.title: No action on babies losing vision despite panel finding hospital negligent
points: Three years have passed since two premature infants suffered irreversible vision loss due to medical negligence, yet legal recourse remains unaddressed.
Investigations by the West Bengal Medical Council and a local committee established doctors’ culpability for negligence and manipulation of records.
Baby Mivaan Choudhary lost vision in his left eye due to the lack of timely ROP screening.

items.title: AI to break language barriers in accessing govt welfare schemes
points: Citizens can now access the ministry of social justice's digital services in over 22 languages, thanks to an innovative AI-powered chatbot designed to assist users effectively.
This initiative strives to overcome challenges posed by fragmented information and language barriers.
The advanced AI will also improve translation and speech support, marking a substantial advancement in promoting inclusive welfare for diverse language communities.

items.title: Baler isn’t a bailout: Why stubble subsidies still bypass small farmers
points: Stubble burning has sharply declined in Punjab and Haryana due to Government interventions, yet many farmers still burn residue.
The critical 10-day window between crops often leads to hasty decisions among farmers without access to machinery.
While some farmers benefit from private baling businesses and government subsidies, others face structural barriers to accessing these services.
Issues include machinery availability, high costs, and delays in subsidies affecting smallholders disproportionately.

items.title: Kharif output in 2026-27 dips amid deficient monsoon, but still better than 5-year average; 2025-26 crop year, however, reports record output of foodgrains
points: Recent preliminary estimates from the agriculture ministry indicate a decline in kharif foodgrain production caused by insufficient rainfall.
Last year's foodgrain output reached an impressive record of 378 million tonnes, well above previous figures.
Major crops like paddy and maize may face reduced yields this season due to various agricultural difficulties.

items.title: Why Centre called Parliament session after over 100-day gap; delimitation bill in focus, opposition worried
points: The government has declared that Parliament will reconvene on November 30 to discuss the delimitation bill.
This has raised alarms among opposition groups who are wary of the implications for electoral districts and voter lists.
The Congress Party has voiced dissatisfaction over the late announcement of winter session dates, recalling a past failed Constitution amendment concerning delimitation due to insufficient backing.

items.title: ‘Generally stable’: China on border with India amid troop build-up reports, reiterates claim over Arunachal Pradesh
points: China's military reported that the situation along the India-China border is currently stable and communication is ongoing.
High-level military talks addressed recent troop build-up concerns in Arunachal Pradesh, particularly in the Upper Subansiri region.
China reasserted its claim over the Arunachal Pradesh territory, calling it Zangnan, despite India's opposition.
Simultaneously, concerns were raised regarding India-Japan defense cooperation, which China criticized.

items.title: ‘Zero tolerance for terror’: Amit Shah says India leading global fight against terrorism
Meta vs Congress: Why opposition party is up in arms against the tech giant
points: Congress has taken legal action against Meta and the Indian government by filing a petition in the Delhi high court.
They assert that the automated system for blocking content is hindering the dissemination of legitimate political messages relating to Rahul Gandhi, including innocent birthday wishes and tributes.
This, they argue, threatens transparent communication with voters prior to the forthcoming elections.
The high court is set to commence hearings soon.

items.title: Government calls for special Parliament session from November 30 amid buzz over delimitation bill
points: The government has scheduled special parliamentary sessions to address essential business starting November 30, 2026.
Discussions will include the government's plans for delimitation and women's reservation.
The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill had previously failed to secure the required majority in Lok Sabha.
There are growing concerns among opposition parties regarding the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.
Ministers have been asked to prepare for these upcoming parliamentary discussions and debates.

items.title: BharatGen launches Patram 1.5, AI model that reads, understands and reasons over documents
points: BharatGen has introduced Patram 1.5, a vision-language model designed for enhanced document reading and processing.
This new model, termed ‘OCR 3.0’, combines image understanding and reasoning to interpret mixed-language documents.
It enables users to extract specific information and flags ambiguous or illegible fields.
Evaluations compared it with numerous other AI and OCR models, highlighting its local benchmarks.
The technology supports sensitive document processing for banks, hospitals, and government agencies.

items.title: World Hindu Congress 2026 to draw 4,500 delegates from 60 countries in Mumbai
points: In Mumbai next month, the fourth World Hindu Congress is set to convene, welcoming over 4,500 delegates from more than 60 nations.
The event’s objective is to unite the global Hindu community to tackle significant issues and share perspectives.
Notably, the congress will debut the World Hindu Expo, aimed at fostering economic development within this community, alongside various discussions spanning business and political sectors.

items.title: 'Abdul won't lay carpets': Chandrashekhar Azad, Asaduddin Owaisi promise Muslim deputy CM in UP
India's first museum dedicated to Chief Justices of India inaugurated at OP Jindal Global University in Sonipat
points: A museum dedicated to the Chief Justices of India was inaugurated at OP Jindal Global University in Sonipat.
The museum features over 280 busts of judges and displays on landmark judgments.
It aims to document the evolution of the Supreme Court and constitutional governance in India.
The inauguration coincided with Constitution Day, emphasizing the importance of judicial contributions to democracy.

items.title: PDA quota, dole for jobless, caste survey: Decoding Akhilesh Yadav's big manifesto promises for UP
points: Akhilesh Yadav has unveiled an ambitious manifesto for the upcoming 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, focusing on creating 25 lakh government jobs and providing Rs 5,000 monthly assistance for unemployed graduates.
The manifesto champions caste representation and women's safety while fostering a diverse coalition.
Additional proposals include waiving farmers' loans and investing substantially in rural infrastructure, particularly targeting the youth and various communities in Uttar Pradesh.
